newsitem.title: LATVIA: Gazprom asks for Latvia Gas selloff postponement.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom asks for Latvia Gas selloff postponement.

text.p: Russian gas giant Gazprom has asked for the deadline for it sign an agreement on buying a stake in Latvian Gas to be extended to March, the Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) said on Thursday.
LPA director general Janis Naglis told Reuters that Gazprom asked for the delay as it wanted to clarify the financial situation of Latvian Gas.
Naglis said Latvia had not yet answered the Russian demand to extend the deadline but would do so later today.
"Our delegation has been to Moscow and thoroughly discussed the financial issues," Naglis said.
"The remaining thing now is for the Gazprom board is to decide whether to buy a stake in Latvian Gas," Naglis said.
He added that clarifications on the share purchase contract have also been sent to Moscow.
Latvia has also had problems with German investors Ruhrgas and Preussen, who are seeking government guarantees for all of Latvian Gas's debts.

The LPA has extended the deadline for the German firms to sign a purchase agreement until April 1 to give the Latvian government time to make a decision on writing off and capitalising the Latvian Gas debts.
